title: Sandbox conformance case
description: One case, of two kinds. A `harness` case is the decision table written down: permissions and platform in, an ordered sequence of probe invocations out, driven through a stubbed probe runner. A `classify` case drives the pure errno-to-exit-code mapping, which is the one part of a probe's own logic reproducible without a real sandbox.

platform.description: harness only. The value of the harness's platform option.

permissions.description: harness only. The manifest's `permissions` member, verbatim — any JSON value, because the harness must tolerate the legacy array form, null, and an absent object without failing.

probeResults.description: harness only. Exit code the stubbed runner returns for each probe name. A probe the case does not declare here MUST NOT be invoked; the runner treats an undeclared invocation as a case authoring error.

calls.description: Every probe invocation, in order. An empty array asserts the harness invoked nothing.

failingProbe.description: When the outcome is `throw`, the probe the error message must name. A binding that throws for the wrong reason otherwise passes.

classifier.description: classify only. Which of the two error-code sets applies.

code.description: classify only. The error's code, or null for an error carrying none — the case that made the Bun.file defect silent, and the one a binding is most likely to leave undefined.

expectExit.description: classify only. The exit code the classification must produce.
